To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Indices of macrovascular and skin microvascular endothelial functions are independently related to cardiovascular mortality risk, 2) The agreement between the methods representing different vascular bed is weak, and 3) The indices are not interchangeable
endothelial dysfunction, measured by different non-invasive methods in different vascular beds and related to cardiovascular risk, may not be interchangeable.

(i) indices of macrovascular (flow-mediated dilation and pulse wave reflection) and microvascular endothelium-dependent vasodilation (cutaneous laser Doppler flux) relate to cardiovascular mortality, but not to cardiac target organ injury, and (ii) the different vascular beds show only little interrelation, which may depend upon different pathogenetic mechanism.
